overview: China Overseas Land & Investment (COLI) is a Hong Kong-listed, Beijing/Hong Kong-headquartered property developer and one of the largest state-backed real estate groups in China, majority-owned (~56%) by China Overseas Holdings Limited, itself wholly owned by China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC), a centrally administered state-owned enterprise. The Group develops and sells residential and mixed-use property across roughly 84 Chinese mainland cities plus Hong Kong and Macau, while also owning and operating a growing commercial portfolio of offices, shopping malls, hotels and leased apartments in the Chinese mainland, Hong Kong, Macau and London. It consolidates China Overseas Grand Oceans Group (COGO) and holds an associate stake used for lower-tier-city development, giving it a combined "Group Series of Companies" sales footprint that the China Index Academy ranks No.1 in the industry by attributable contracted sales.

business_model.summary: Primarily a residential/mixed-use property developer (property development was ~93% of FY2025 revenue) generating largely project-based, lumpy revenue recognized on unit handover, supplemented by a smaller but growing recurring-income commercial operations segment (offices, malls, hotels, leased apartments) and other businesses including material procurement/supply-chain services for the broader CSCEC ecosystem. FY2025 revenue was RMB168.09bn (-9.2% YoY): property development RMB156.77bn, commercial properties RMB7.2bn, other businesses the remainder. H1 2026 revenue was RMB97.6bn with property development RMB91.86bn and commercial operations RMB3.58bn (office RMB1.72bn, malls RMB1.16bn, leased apartments RMB0.18bn, hotels/other RMB0.52bn). The Group is state-directed in capital allocation and credit access, ranked No.1 in the industry for newly acquired land premium in FY2025 (RMB118.69bn total, RMB92.42bn attributable) even as peers retrenched, reflecting its funding-cost advantage and policy role in stabilizing the sector.

revenue_streams.name: Property development (residential/mixed-use sales)
revenue_streams.trend: declining - FY2025 revenue -10.3% YoY on sector downturn, though contracted sales ranked No.1 in industry

revenue_streams.name: Commercial property operations (office, retail, hotel, leased apartments)
revenue_streams.trend: growing modestly - FY2025 commercial revenue +1.0% YoY; office occupancy 78%, malls 95.3% occupancy with same-store sales +4.5% YoY in H1 2026

revenue_streams.name: Other operations (material procurement/supply chain, other services)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - H1 2026 external supply-chain revenue +35% YoY

business_model.customer_type: B2C (residential home buyers across first-, second- and selected lower-tier Chinese mainland cities plus Hong Kong and Macau) and B2B (corporate office/retail tenants, hotel operators, and intra-group/external supply-chain customers)
business_model.geographic_mix: Chinese mainland is the overwhelming majority of revenue and land bank (Northern Region RMB55.19bn, Eastern Region RMB45.69bn, Southern Region RMB36.97bn, Central/Western RMB17.96bn of FY2025 property development revenue), with Hong Kong, Macau and a small London commercial asset as secondary markets; first-tier cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Hong Kong) represented 57.3% of FY2025 Group Series contracted sales (ex-COGO) and 68.6% in H1 2026, reflecting a deliberate 'flight to safety' strategy

main_competitors: Sun Hung Kai Properties / Kerry Properties (Hong Kong overlap)
surviving private developers (e.g., Country Garden, Sunac) now largely in distress or restructuring
competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest and most financially sound developers in China by attributable sales (China Index Academy ranks the Group Series of Companies No.1 in the industry for several consecutive years); among a small handful of 'green category' (top credit-tier) developers still able to access low-cost onshore and offshore funding at scale while many private peers are in default or restructuring

moat_factors.description: Majority owned (~56%) by China Overseas Holdings Limited, wholly owned by CSCEC, a centrally administered SOE; this parentage underpins credit ratings, access to bank credit lines (RMB49.5bn unutilised facilities at 1H2026) and a policy-favored role as a 'systemically important' stabilizing force in a sector where many private developers have defaulted

Average borrowing cost of 2.76% at 1H2026 (down from 2.8% FY2025, 3.8%+ at smaller/private peers), among the lowest in the industry; remains the only listed Chinese property developer rated A- by two of the three major agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch), enabling continued bond issuance (including a 15-year note at 2.5%, the first of its tenor in the domestic market) even as most private developers are shut out of capital markets

Deliberate concentration in first-tier cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Hong Kong = 73.9% of FY2025 attributable land premium) gives pricing resilience and faster sell-through versus lower-tier/private peers; total land reserve 37.27m sq m (Group, FY2025) plus COGO's reserve for lower-tier-city optionality

No.1 ranked attributable sales nationally and market-share leader in numerous individual cities (Beijing, Shenzhen, Tianjin, Jinan, Shenyang, etc.); 'China Overseas Good Houses' product standard and strong delivery/customer-satisfaction metrics (industry-benchmark satisfaction scores, No.1 annual delivery capability per CRIC) support premium positioning versus distressed private developers

First consumption-infrastructure REIT (China Overseas Commercial REIT, 180607.SZ, listed Oct 2025 on Shenzhen Exchange, oversubscribed ~100x) opens a securitization channel to recycle capital from mature commercial assets into new development, a capability most peers lack at this stage

weaknesses: Still heavily exposed to a structurally declining Chinese mainland residential market (national new-home sales projected to fall a further ~6% in 2026 per S&P) despite being a 'best-in-class' operator within that market

Profitability has compressed sharply even for a sector leader - gross margin down from ~38% (FY2018) to 15.5% (FY2025), underlying/core profit down 17-22% in each of the last two full-year/half-year periods, reflecting lower average selling prices and intensified competition even among surviving developers
Commercial/recurring-income base, while growing, remains small relative to the development business (~4% of revenue) and is not yet large enough to offset cyclicality in sales

State-directed capital allocation, while a funding advantage, also means strategic decisions (e.g., aggressive land acquisition in a down market) can be influenced by policy/stabilization mandates rather than purely shareholder-return optimization

Reliance on China Index Academy/CRIC third-party rankings and 'Group Series of Companies' (including non-wholly-owned COGO and JVs) for headline sales figures can overstate the economic interest attributable to COLI shareholders

growth_drivers: Continued market-share consolidation as weaker private developers exit or restructure, allowing COLI to deploy its funding-cost advantage into land acquisition at a point when competitors are capital-constrained (FY2025: RMB118.69bn total land premium, No.1 in industry; 18 new parcels acquired YTD 2026 for RMB33.34bn attributable premium as of the H1 2026 report date)

'Dual-engine' strategy strengthening the commercial operations business via new REIT issuances (following the October 2025 China Overseas Commercial REIT listing) to recycle capital from mature office/mall/hotel/apartment assets, with office buildings, hotels and leased apartments now within the scope of eligible REIT asset classes per recent policy changes

First-tier city concentration strategy positioned to benefit disproportionately if/when the government's 'three driving forces' thesis (stable macro growth, policy support/supply-demand rebalancing, and COLI's own balanced growth-resilience positioning) plays out, with early signs of price/volume recovery already visible in Shanghai, Shenzhen and the Hong Kong Kai Tak Runway Area project

Structural policy support for 'Good Houses' quality upgrade and urban village/dilapidated housing renovation, which favors well-capitalized, high-quality-product developers like COLI over distressed peers, alongside a March 2026 Ministry of Natural Resources policy restricting new commercial land supply (reducing competitive overbuilding)
Elderly care/senior living platform (China Overseas Senior Living and Wellness, Beijing Jinchen project opened H1 2026) as an early-stage adjacency tapping into China's 'silver economy' demand

Continued deleveraging (net gearing 27.2% at 1H2026, down from 34.2% FY2025 and 42.9% FY2022) creating balance-sheet capacity for further selective, counter-cyclical acquisitions and buybacks of higher-cost debt

business.description: National new-home sales have declined for multiple consecutive years and S&P projects a further ~6% decline in 2026 primary sales value; COLI's own FY2025 contracted sales fell 19.1% YoY and property development revenue fell 10.3% YoY despite its best-in-class positioning

Gross margin has fallen from ~38% (FY2018) to 15.5% (FY2025) and operating margin from ~41% to ~12%, driven by lower average selling prices, inventory/land cost legacy and intensifying 'flight to quality' competition even among surviving developers

Large stock of properties/inventories (RMB491bn at FY2025) carries valuation risk if the downturn persists or deepens, particularly in lower-tier cities and COGO-linked projects outside the core five first-tier markets

business.risk: Dependence on JV/associate (COGO) and lower-tier-city exposure
business.description: COGO contributed 14.3% of H1 2026 Group Series contracted sales but operates largely in weaker lower-tier cities, a structurally softer segment of the market than COLI's core first-tier concentration

financial.description: Total debt of RMB237.2bn at 1H2026 (RMB162.15bn bank loans, RMB75.07bn notes/bonds), with RMB64.86bn (27.3%) maturing within one year; continuous refinancing dependence even for a top-tier credit

87.7% of debt and the great majority of revenue/assets are RMB-denominated (reporting currency is also RMB), limiting translation risk versus HKD/USD-reporting HK peers, but the ~10% USD-denominated notes and dividend conversion to HKD for shareholders creates residual FX exposure; management states it relies on natural hedging with no derivative speculation

Core profit attributable to shareholders fell 17.2% in FY2025 and underlying 1H2026 core profit remained under pressure; interest coverage ratio has nearly halved from 7.2x (FY2021) to 2.8x (FY2025), reducing the earnings buffer against further margin erosion

regulatory.risk: Post-'three red lines' regulatory legacy and ongoing deleveraging mandates
regulatory.description: Although enforcement has evolved since the original 2020-21 'three red lines' (debt-to-asset, net gearing, cash-to-short-term-debt) policy, developer leverage, pre-sale fund escrow rules and land-financing reforms continue to shape sector financing conditions and COLI's own reported liability-to-asset ratio (51.6% at 1H2026) and net gearing metrics

As an SOE subsidiary used partly as a policy instrument to stabilize the property sector, COLI's land acquisition pace and pricing discipline may at times be influenced by national/local stabilization objectives rather than purely shareholder-value optimization, a risk cited implicitly in its aggressive land-bank growth (RMB118.69bn FY2025 land premium) during a down-cycle

regulatory.risk: New land-use policy restricting commercial development
regulatory.description: March 2026 Ministry of Natural Resources policy that newly allocated construction land shall generally not be used for commercial property development could constrain future commercial-segment land supply/optionality, though management frames it as net positive for controlling oversupply

macro.risk: Local government land sales slump and fiscal stress
macro.description: Chinese local governments' land-sale revenue, historically a major fiscal source, has slumped alongside the broader property downturn, constraining local government capacity for market-support measures (subsidies, infrastructure that underpins new project viability) even as developers like COLI continue large land acquisitions

The broader Chinese developer sector continues to see defaults and distress among major private players; while COLI itself is insulated as a top-tier SOE credit, continued industry-wide weakness in sales (top-100 developer sales -27% YoY in January 2026 per S&P) depresses buyer confidence and comparable pricing sector-wide

macro.risk: Household wealth/'poverty effect' and consumer sentiment
macro.description: Years of falling home prices have dented Chinese household wealth and consumption confidence broadly, a lingering drag on housing demand recovery even as policy support (purchase-restriction easing in Beijing/Shanghai, VAT relief, provident fund loan limit increases) accumulates

macro.risk: Interest rate and monetary policy sensitivity
macro.description: Mortgage rates, developer funding costs and cap rates on investment property are all sensitive to PBOC policy; COLI's effective borrowing cost has fallen with the rate-cutting cycle (2.76% at 1H2026) but a pause or reversal (US Fed paused cuts in 1H2026 per the interim report) could pressure both funding costs and demand

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese mainland new-home sales are forecast to decline a further ~6% in 2026 (S&P Global), with the sector still searching for a bottom after a multi-year correction; however policymakers (city-specific purchase-restriction easing in Beijing/Shanghai, provident-fund loan limit increases, VAT relief on second-hand transactions, land-supply controls) are incrementally supportive, and first-tier cities (COLI's core focus) are showing earlier signs of stabilization/price recovery than the national market. Hong Kong residential has also been inflecting positively in 2026
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - both the development sales business (driven by rates, local policy, household sentiment, land-market dynamics) and the smaller commercial portfolio (corporate occupier demand, cap rates) are classically cyclical, rate- and sentiment-sensitive real estate businesses, compounded in China's case by a multi-year structural deleveraging of the broader sector
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - average borrowing cost (2.76% at 1H2026) and debt refinancing terms move with PBOC and global rate policy; mortgage affordability for buyers and cap rates for the commercial portfolio are similarly rate-sensitive
key_input_costs: Land premiums/land acquisition costs (RMB118.69bn total FY2025 land spend)

recent_developments.event: 1H2026 interim results: revenue RMB97.6bn, profit attributable to shareholders RMB7.03bn, core profit RMB7.93bn, basic EPS RMB0.64 (missed consensus ~RMB0.68 per Investing.com); contracted sales RMB134.35bn (+11.8% YoY) ranked No.1 in the industry; net gearing improved to 27.2% from 34.2% at FY2025 year-end; interim dividend HK23 cents declared

Acquired nine further land parcels in Beijing, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Taiyuan and Ningbo for RMB25.68bn attributable premium, bringing year-to-date 2026 land acquisitions to 18 parcels / RMB33.34bn attributable premium, continuing aggressive counter-cyclical land banking
Beijing Jinchen senior-living project opened under China Overseas Senior Living and Wellness brand, an early step into China's elderly-care/'silver economy' adjacency

Ministry of Natural Resources issued policy that newly allocated construction land generally cannot be used for commercial property development, aimed at reducing new commercial oversupply; Beijing and Shanghai further relaxed home purchase restrictions in late 2025/early 2026

FY2025 annual results: revenue RMB168.09bn (-9.2% YoY), profit attributable to shareholders RMB12.69bn (-18.9%), core profit RMB13.01bn (-17.2%); contracted sales RMB251.23bn (-19.1%) still ranked No.1 in the industry; net gearing rose to 34.2% from 29.2%; full-year dividend cut 16.7% to HK50 cents; land acquisitions of RMB118.69bn (total) led the industry

China Overseas Commercial REIT (Huaxia/CAMC-managed, 180607.SZ) listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange - the Group's first consumption-infrastructure REIT, oversubscribed roughly 100x, marking a new asset-recycling/capital-light monetization channel for the commercial portfolio

Analyst coverage remained broadly constructive (consensus skewing Buy across trackers, e.g., Investing.com showing 15 Buy/1 Hold among 16 analysts, average 12-month target ~HK$19; Goldman Sachs Buy/HK$16.80 Aug-2026, JPMorgan Buy/HK$19.50 May-2026), though targets and estimates have been trimmed through the year alongside sector-wide sales weakness and the 1H2026 EPS miss

Broader China property sector context: S&P Global flagged rising industry-wide liquidity risk for 2026 and a further ~6% decline in primary home sales nationally; top-100 developer sales fell ~27% YoY in January 2026, underscoring that even a top-tier SOE developer like COLI is operating against a still-deteriorating sector backdrop

items.target: continued reduction toward a 'reasonable' / prudent level
items.notes: No specific numeric target disclosed; net gearing improved to 27.2% at 1H2026 from 34.2% at FY2025 year-end and 29.2% at FY2024 year-end, continuing a multi-year deleveraging trend management reiterates will continue

items.target: continue counter-cyclical, prime-location land acquisition while maintaining 'green category' credit status
items.notes: RMB33.34bn attributable land premium spent year-to-date through the H1 2026 report date across 18 parcels; management frames this as capturing opportunities while competitors are capital-constrained

items.target: establish additional REIT platforms through continuous injection of mature commercial assets
items.vs_prior: new initiative following Oct-2025 REIT listing
items.notes: No specific asset list, size, or timeline disclosed; framed as a strategic priority to unlock commercial asset value and support the 'dual-engine' development/operations model

items.target: step up both sales and investment efforts, targeting record-high Hong Kong sales
items.notes: Management explicitly states confidence in achieving record-high sales in Hong Kong as that market stabilizes and bounces back, following HK contracted sales of RMB22.23bn in FY2025 (first time ranking 5th by sales in the HK market) and HK contributing over 80% of some recent period's contracted sales mix

items.target: Interim dividend of HK23 cents declared for 1H2026
items.notes: Down from HK25 cents in 1H2025; FY2025 full-year dividend was also cut 16.7% to HK50 cents (from HK60 cents FY2024), reflecting the decline in core profit, a continuation of the downward dividend trend since the FY2021 peak of HK121 cents

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Yan Jianguo's FY2025 and 1H2026 statements describe the property market as 'still adjusting' but lay out a 'three driving forces' thesis for eventual stabilization: (1) steady Chinese macroeconomic growth supporting housing demand, (2) policy support and improving supply-demand balance (purchase-restriction easing, land-supply controls, urban renewal acceleration), and (3) the Group's own 'balanced endogenous driving force combining growth with resilience' - its prime-location land bank, low funding costs, and dual-engine development/commercial-operations model. Management highlights three 'new sources of momentum' as of 1H2026: appreciation of premium first-tier-city assets, structural opportunities in select second-tier cities via a 'prime locations + benchmark projects' strategy, and unlocking commercial asset value via REITs. The company continues to position itself as the industry's most resilient, highest-credit-quality developer even as it acknowledges a still-declining headline market.

bull_case: State-backed, top-tier credit status (one of only a handful of Chinese developers still rated A- territory, the lowest borrowing cost in the industry at 2.76%) allows COLI to keep acquiring prime land and issuing low-cost debt (including an industry-first 15-year domestic bond at 2.5%) precisely when most private-sector competitors are capital-constrained or defaulting - a classic 'survive and consolidate' setup

Deliberate first-tier-city concentration (57-69% of contracted sales) positions COLI to disproportionately benefit from any China property stabilization, since policymakers and most forecasters expect first-tier cities to lead any recovery out of the downturn, with early positive signs already visible in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hong Kong's Kai Tak project

Deleveraging is real and continuing (net gearing down from 42.9% in FY2022 to 27.2% at 1H2026), alongside a new REIT monetization channel (China Overseas Commercial REIT, ~100x oversubscribed) that opens a capital-recycling path for the commercial portfolio independent of the weak development-sales cycle

Remains the No.1-ranked developer in China by attributable contracted sales for multiple consecutive periods even amid a severe sector downturn, demonstrating relative market-share gains versus distressed and defaulted peers (Country Garden, Sunac, etc.), which should compound if the sector consolidates around surviving state-backed players

Analyst sentiment remains constructively skewed toward Buy across major covering brokers (Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Citi-equivalent coverage) with price targets meaningfully above trading levels for parts of 2026, alongside a still-positive (if reduced) dividend
bear_case: Profitability has deteriorated structurally even for the sector's best-positioned operator - gross margin fell from ~38% (FY2018) to 15.5% (FY2025), core profit down 17% (FY2025) and 1H2026 EPS missed consensus, showing that 'best in a bad industry' still means declining earnings, not insulation from the downturn

The Chinese mainland residential market remains in structural decline with no confirmed bottom (S&P projects a further ~6% sales decline in 2026, local-government land-sale revenue under continued stress), and COLI's own contracted sales fell 19.1% in FY2025 despite its No.1 industry ranking

Aggressive counter-cyclical land acquisition (RMB118.69bn FY2025, continuing into 2026) raises execution risk if the downturn is deeper or longer than management's 'three driving forces' stabilization thesis assumes, potentially trapping capital in a still-falling market

Interest coverage has nearly halved since FY2021 (7.2x to 2.8x by FY2025) and total debt remains substantial (RMB237bn at 1H2026) with ongoing refinancing needs, leaving less earnings buffer against further margin or sales declines even with a low average borrowing cost

Dividend has been cut for multiple consecutive periods (FY2021 peak of HK121 cents down to HK50 cents FY2025, 1H2026 interim cut further to HK23 cents from HK25 cents), signaling management's own reduced confidence in near-term earnings recovery despite public optimism in its chairman's statements

As a state-owned policy instrument, COLI's land-buying and market behavior may at times prioritize national/local property-market stabilization objectives over pure shareholder-value optimization, a dynamic that is difficult for minority shareholders to monitor or discipline
